source_user: Advanced cluster case NVIDIA Dynamo-81: Design an evaluation of NVIDIA Dynamo for disaggregated inference orchestration. Variant 81 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: separate frontend routing, prefill workers, decode workers, KV movement, transport overhead, scheduling policy, queueing, model compatibility, observability, and failover behavior. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer: Assume a fixed model/checkpoint, tokenizer, precision, software build, GPU/NIC/NUMA topology, RDMA configuration, prompt and output-length distributions, arrival process, batching, parallelism, and routing policy; record all versions and units. Treat Dynamo as a hypothesis, not a guaranteed speedup: define frontend routing, prefill/decode ownership, scheduling, queueing, KV format/compatibility and transfer path, admission/backpressure, cancellation, retries, observability, and failover semantics. Hypothesis: under matched workload and output quality, disaggregated orchestration reduces TTFT or improves throughput/ITL tails versus a matched local or conventional-distributed baseline without exceeding KV-transfer, queueing, error, or recovery budgets. Run randomized repeated paired trials over short/long prompts, burst rates, worker imbalance, and warm/cold conditions; measure TTFT and ITL p50/p95/p99, requests and tokens/s, queue wait/depth, prefill/decode utilization, batch sizes, KV bytes and transfer latency, rejects, errors, cancellations, duplicate/lost requests, and recovery time, each with units, sample counts, and confidence intervals. Correlate request traces across frontend, workers, transport, and GPUs; test frontend/prefill/decode/transport loss and network degradation with bounded retries and no unsafe replay. Roll back or stop canary if tail SLO, error rate, output equivalence, KV-transfer budget, or recovery objective fails. Evidence required: raw trace and counter data, matched-baseline analysis, fault-test results, compatibility matrix, and independent reproduction; do not claim benefit from estimates or vendor defaults.

source_user: Advanced cluster case multi-node NCCL-4: A multi-node NCCL job hangs only at larger world sizes. Produce a falsifiable diagnosis and rollback plan. Variant 4 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: test rank mapping, interface selection, topology, NIC affinity, rendezvous, firewall and ports, timeout logs, communicator formation, reduced-world baselines, and network counters. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer: Assume the model, NCCL/CUDA/driver versions, world-size and rank mapping, GPU/NIC/NUMA topology, transport (InfiniBand or RoCE), interface selection, container permissions, rendezvous settings, firewall/ports, and workload are known and recorded. Hypothesis: the hang is caused by a scale-dependent communicator or network-path defect—such as inconsistent interface/NIC selection, unreachable port, topology/affinity mismatch, or exhausted connection/resource limit—rather than an application deadlock. Reproduce at the smallest failing world size and bisect rank mappings, hosts, interfaces, NICs, and TP/PP/EP groups against a reduced-world control. Collect per-rank NCCL logs with timestamps, rendezvous and timeout locations, communicator progress, selected interfaces, topology, CUDA errors, link/port state, retransmits, packet/ECN or IB counters, bandwidth, CPU/GPU/NIC affinity, and process/resource limits; report units and sample counts. Validate every rank can resolve and connect to the intended peers, use a known-good transport path, and compare identical software/configuration with only one factor changed. Stop and roll back the new topology, transport, or scale configuration if the reduced-world baseline regresses, ranks cannot form a communicator within the timeout, data-integrity checks fail, or repeated canaries reproduce hangs. Evidence required: failing and passing logs, rank/interface/topology maps, network counters, reproduction matrix, and a tested rollback plus bounded timeout policy; avoid inferring root cause from a single timeout.
